candidate_analysis.explanation: The Random Forest labels this binary as malware with probability 1.0000, and all 20 top n-grams push toward cryptojacking. Their SHAP contributions are tightly clustered (+0.0066 to +0.0115), so no single feature dominates. Most of the evidence is generic compiler-generated stack and calling-convention code: CALL PUSH (0.0354 frequency), MOV PUSH (0.0421), PUSH CALL (0.0505), ADD PUSH, SUB PUSH, POP PUSH, INC PUSH, MOVZX PUSH, MOV LEAVE, CALL RET and PUSH RET. These appear in nearly all native x86 binaries and do not indicate mining behavior. A few rare n-grams are somewhat more suggestive of bit-level or multi-precision arithmetic, which can occur in hashing or crypto loops: CMP SHLD (0.008157), SBB INC (0.009395) and SHL NEG (0.006918). They are very low frequency (about 0.00002-0.0001), though, and the evidence does not show which functions contain them. Rare register-restore sequences (POP XOR, POP LEA, POP OR, POP SUB, POP CMP, POP CALL) may reflect function epilogues or obfuscated or packed code, but nothing in the evidence confirms that. The evidence has no function-level context, no named routines and no mining-specific artifacts. The malware classification is therefore well supported statistically, but the cryptojacking-specific interpretation is only partly supported. That puts this in the low-confidence tier rather than high-confidence.

Check for packing or obfuscation, and look for mining-related network or configuration artifacts before assigning a high-confidence cryptojacking verdict.
